title: Cost bound for a sequence of programs
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, choose a learning access mode and an output type, and let $T$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose $P$ assigns a natural number to each learning cost, with $P(0)=0$ and $P(c+d)=P(c)+P(d)$ for all learning costs $c,d$. If, for every program in a finite list and every outcome-cost pair in the support of that program's run under $T$, the value of $P$ on its cost is at most $B$, then every outcome-cost pair in the support of the run of the whole sequence has cost projection at most the length of the list times $B$.
hypotheses_covered: A learning access mode and output type
A Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
A cost projection from learning costs to natural numbers
The projection maps zero cost to zero
The projection is additive on all pairs of learning costs
Each listed program's supported outcomes have projected cost at most $B
The specified sequence outcome-cost pair is in the sequence run's support
